who: the steward's clerk and a scribe

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Forty bushels in, thirty-eight in the ledger. Where did two go?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Rats, the granary boy says.

lines.text: {steward} wants the shortfall in red ink.

lines.speaker: B

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then use less of it. Small letters.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Strike {hamlet}'s tithe for this quarter.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Struck, or owed?

lines.speaker: B

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That headland's gone to thistle. Whose strip is it?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The lord's. Nobody weeds what they don't eat.

lines.text: They'll weed it Thursday, or the fine goes in the book.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Count the stooks before the reeve's cousins do.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You think I'd let them thieve under my nose?

lines.text: I think you've a great many cousins.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Ash on the barley ears. See it?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Smut, surely. Wet summer.

lines.speaker: A

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then the village strips rot standing.

lines.text: Table by the fire wants more ale.

lines.text: Guildsmen from {guild} in the corner. Mind your purse.

lines.text: {player} was in again. Asked my name.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Asked mine too. Leaves a coin and says thanks.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Strange sort. I like it.

lines.speaker: A

lines.text: And the hamlet losing sheep to wolves gets the antlers to look at.

lines.text: And burns. The Crows torch the thatch now.
